name: Klonis
caption: A newcomer who won the promotion's own second King of Inferno battle royal and used it to challenge for, and fall short of, the Buckeye Championship.

tenures.source: Billed the reigning King of Inferno, challenging “Mr. Charisma” Christian York for the OWF Buckeye Championship on the promotion's own 10 January 1999 broadcast and losing.

name: “Sick & Twisted” Zack Sharp
caption: A hardcore-styled challenger who fought Christian York to a finish not preserved in the surviving record, in a match for the promotion's own vacant Buckeye Championship.

tenures.source: Billed challenging “Mr. Charisma” Christian York for the vacant OWF Buckeye Championship in the main event of the promotion's own Second Coming pay-per-view; the match's own decisive fall does not survive the record.

identity.note: The same nickname and name recur on a NEWC wrestler; nothing in this promotion's own record links the two.

name: Fang
caption: A three-time Akron City champion whose second reign began off the surviving record and ended at the promotion's own Second Coming, and who later fell short in a first-blood challenge for the Buckeye title.

tenures.source: Billed OWF Akron City Champion entering the promotion's own Second Coming pay-per-view, where he lost the title to Aaron Farner; later challenged Christian York for the Buckeye Championship at Spring Strife: Birthday Bash and lost by first blood.
the promotion's own 9 February 2001 Event Center and 12 March 2001 Ring Wars
Billed as special guest referee for the Battle of the Ages on the event's own lineup of 2 June 2002; the event was called off before it was held.

identity.note: A common masked-wrestler ring name recurring across four other held wings; nothing in this promotion's own record links any of them to this wrestler specifically.
Shares a common ring name with wrestlers billed by many other independently-run promotions; no document links this MVW persona to any of them.
A shared ring name only: wrestlers billed Fang in other wings and polls, with no billing, roster, opponent or document tying any of them to the GSWP, OWF and MVW Fang.

Pending a verdict. The 1998 RSPWF Top 200's #66 Fang (tagged MVW, EWC, LAW, GCW, HHWO) and the 1999 list's #8 (tagged GSWP, EMWC, WWO) are this Fang on the handler's own signatures ('#66 '98 RSPWF Poll' in 1999; '#8 '99 RSPWF 200' on 23 January 2000, /promotions/rspwf/archive/critique-discussion-fang-rp-2000-01-23.html), and the GSWP's video package of 4 April 1999 shows him on EWC Wednesday Wreckage; but that poll record also holds the same 1998 list's #117 Fang (tagged POW, AWMC) and an AWMC run, a second Fang, so it needs a split before any fold.

name: “Flashy” Michael Robinson
caption: The Akron City Champion who won the title from Joey Jackson and lost it, off the surviving record, during the promotion's own closing card.

tenures.source: Won the OWF Akron City Championship from “The Word” Joey Jackson on the promotion's own 15 November 1998 Sunday Inferno; billed defending it against Fang at the promotion's own closing SnowScraps: Termination card, whose results do not survive.
Lost his first-round match on the tournament's second edition, 23 February 1999.

identity.note: A shared full name with an unrelated wrestler in another held wing; no corroborating axis, so the collision is recorded distinct.

name: “The Word” Joey Jackson
caption: The promotion's own first billed Akron City Champion, who lost the title early in the surviving record and stayed on the roster as a recurring midcard wrestler.

tenures.source: Billed OWF Akron City Champion before losing the title to “Flashy” Michael Robinson on the promotion's own 15 November 1998 Sunday Inferno, reported in the promotion's own 21 January 1999 newsletter; remained active on the roster into 1999.

name: Aaron “Wildfire” Farner
caption: The Akron City Championship's first two-time holder, who won it from Fang, lost it off the surviving record, and reclaimed it in a ladder match.

tenures.source: Won the OWF Akron City Championship from Fang at the promotion's own Second Coming pay-per-view; lost it to Jeremy Steele in a match not preserved in the surviving record, then regained it from Steele in a ladder match on the promotion's own 3 June 1999 broadcast, still champion at the end of the surviving record.

name: Jeremy Steele
caption: A returning wrestler who took the Akron City Championship from Aaron Farner in a match the surviving record does not preserve, then lost it back to him in a ladder match.

tenures.source: Billed as having taken the OWF Akron City Championship from Aaron Farner in a match not preserved in the surviving record; lost the title back to Farner in a ladder match on the promotion's own 3 June 1999 broadcast.

identity.note: The same name recurs on an OSW Online wrestler; nothing in this promotion's own record links the two.

name: “Sudden Death” Shane Matthews
caption: The promotion's own longest-reigning Lightweight Champion, who won the vacant title by forfeit and lost it to outside interference more than five months later.

tenures.source: Won the vacant OWF Lightweight Championship by forfeit from Scott Wright on the promotion's own 15 November 1998 Sunday Inferno; lost the title to “The Human Torture Rack” Ian Walsh on the promotion's own 5 May 1999 broadcast after interference from a manager at ringside.

identity.note: The same billing recurs across three other held wings; nothing in this promotion's own record links any of them to this wrestler specifically.

name: Greg “The Millionaire” Miller
caption: A cocky free agent who challenged for the Lightweight Championship twice and came up short both times.

tenures.source: Billed challenging for the OWF Lightweight Championship on the promotion's own 10 January 1999 and Second Coming broadcasts, losing both.

name: “Confident” Lawrence Williams
caption: The promotion's own on-screen president and a former vice-president, who awarded himself the Lightweight Championship by contract ruling and lost it a week and a half later to a ladder match.

tenures.source: Billed OWF Vice-President in the promotion's own January 1999 newsletter and its own on-screen President by June 1999; ruled a rival wrestler to have forfeited the OWF Lightweight Championship and awarded it to himself on the promotion's own 3 June 1999 broadcast, then lost it to Napoleon in a ladder match at Spring Strife: Birthday Bash.

identity.note: The same billing and nickname recur across three other held wings; nothing in this promotion's own record links any of them to this wrestler specifically.

name: Napoleon
caption: The self-declared leader of the Mini Rebels stable, who won the Lightweight Championship from the promotion's own president in a ladder match by riding the ladder down with the title in hand.

tenures.source: Leader of the Mini Rebels stable, billed from the promotion's own relaunch; won the OWF Lightweight Championship from “Confident” Lawrence Williams in a ladder match at Spring Strife: Birthday Bash, still champion at the end of the surviving record.

name: OWF President
caption: The promotion's own on-screen founder and president, a recurring on-air figure in its rivalry with a New York promotion and its own contract rulings.

tenures.source: The promotion's own on-screen president throughout the surviving record, appearing in the promotion's own rivalry angle with Mohawk Valley Wrestling and narrating the promotion's own history on its broadcasts.

name: "The Saint" Dante Alexander
notes: Known from one application and roleplay posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy on 30 January 1999, titled "[Free Agent] - Dante Alexander - Please Critique. =o)", served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/free-agent-dante-alexander-please-critique-o-1999-01-30.html. The filled-in OWF application makes him a 28-year-old, 6'7", 286-pound heel powerhouse and brawler from "an unknown haven" who enters to Gregorian chants and finishes with the Salvation, a reverse Russian legsweep, after spreading his arms in a human-crucifix pose. In the roleplay he stands in a dark church in a black pastor's suit with his hand on an old book, says some call him a saint and most an outcast because he once offered to heal the sick, and promises to make the OWF his new haven until his work is done.
caption: A 6'7" heel in a pastor's suit who calls himself a saint and preaches from an old church altar in his OWF application, January 1999.
